title: Linked List Cycle

content.problemStatement:
A singly linked list is described by an array `nums`, where `nums[i]`
is the value of the i-th node and node i normally points to node i+1.
You're also given an integer `pos`: the 0-indexed position that the
last node's next pointer connects back to, instead of ending the list
normally. Reason about the list as if you were traversing it node by
node with a next pointer, wrapping around to index `pos` after the
last element when `pos != -1`.

**Determine whether the list has a cycle.**

If `pos` is -1, the list has no cycle and simply ends after the last
node.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: the last node (-4) points back to index 1 (value 2), forming a cycle
the last node (2) points back to index 0 (value 1)
single node, no cycle, the list just ends

hints: Using a dummy head node can simplify edge cases when modifying the head of the list.
Fast and slow pointers (Floyd's cycle-finding algorithm) can help detect cycles or find the middle element in a single pass.
Always update next pointers carefully to avoid creating accidental cycles or losing references to the rest of the list.
